about: Title rules of the MBA role set, written by pipeline/roles_mba.py (do not edit by hand). Patterns are JavaScript regular expressions; use the 'i' flag. How to read a title: see 'how'.
how: 1. A title that matches 'junk' has no role. When the title starts with the first word of the employer's name (four letters or more) and a space, that word is removed first.

2. general = the first entry of 'families' with a match in 'patterns' and none in 'exclude'. ib_associate and corporate_banking are also skipped when the title matches 'tech_staff'. An entry with 'product_gate' also needs the product rules to hold: product.family(title) equals the gate, and product.title_ok(title).

3. big = the employer is in 'big_employers'. When the employer's category is in 'employer_first', general is not in 'named_first' and not big: use the employer rule (step 5) if it gives a role; but when general is not empty and the title matches 'campus_rank' and not 'deal', the role is general.

4. When general is corp_dev, the employer is big or in 'banks', its category is none or Investment banking, and the title does not say corporate development ('corp_dev_named'): the role is ib_associate. Otherwise, when general is not empty, the role is general.

5. Employer rule (the fallback when general is empty): at a consulting category, a title matching 'consultant' is management_consultant unless it matches 'consultant_exclude'. At a Strategy consulting firm, a title matching 'house_rank' is management_consultant unless it matches 'house_staff'. At a 'bank_categories' employer, when the title matches 'deal' and not 'tech_staff', take the 'sector' words out first. Then no role when the title matches 'employer_exclude' (or 'real_estate_exclude' at a real-estate firm); else the first rule of 'employer_rules'[category] that matches. For a big employer the result counts only when the title matches 'deal' or 'campus_rank'.
6. Still no role: 'last_resort'.family when the title matches its pattern.

7. Level: pick the ladder ('ladders'.*.applies), replace a chief-of-staff phrase ('chief_of_staff') with 'CoS', then the first grade whose pattern matches; none: 'mid'. An ldp title with no manager word ('ldp_staff') is 'associate'.
